## Intent
Hypothesis: delegating the Halide-expressible math loop to AOT-compiled code can approach the streaming ceiling even with a scalar respawn loop.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout offers loops with sharply different hot fractions: loop 1 touches 24/68 B (35%), loop 2 only 8/68 B (11%), loop 3 touches 28/68 B (41%) — the rest is dead weight on every stride-68 access. No intermediates: the death verdict stays in registers, so loop 2's 199-instruction body handles RNG, death, and respawn inline. Loop 1 is delegated to an external Halide AOT call (halide_b5_math); loops 2-3 remain scalar. The working set spills L1d at N≈481 and L2 at N≈7710, but with 8-28 hot bytes per particle the effective hot footprint is 3-8x smaller than nominal.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p-vs-N curve is flat across all regimes. At q=0.01, cost rises only 3% from L1d (22.97 ns/p) through L2 (23.59, N=3100); the L2→L3 transition at N≈7700 produces no knee (25.4→25.7). The first real rise comes at L3→DRAM (N≈250000): 24.7→26.9, then 29.4 at N=1M. The 75-199 instruction loop bodies dominate over memory latency at every regime — cache behavior is irrelevant when instruction overhead is this high.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth peaks at 2.96 GB/s — 23% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — against a 5.359 ns/p floor, so the algo runs at 4.3x irreducible memory time even at best. This is overhead-bound: profiles show 63-68% backend stalls and 10-15% branch flushes. Against naive scalar the algo is at parity everywhere (0.997-1.16x). Against the winner it is 2.0-3.7x slower; the gap widens in L3 (3.6x at N=160000, q=0.01) where the winner's packed SIMD streams. At q=0.5 the gap narrows to 2.0x — branchy respawn equalizes.

## Assembly
Codegen is entirely scalar: the 13 vector-suffixed instructions are scalar SSE only (vmovss, vmulss, vucomiss, vcvttss2si) — no packed SIMD. Loop 1 is opaque (call to halide_b5_math). Loop 2 dominates at 199 insns/iter with 21 cond-branches and 12 cmovae for select-based death logic, explaining the 10-15% branch-flush share. The render loop performs byte-granular scatter: each pixel is movzx+add+cmp+cmovae+mov BYTE PTR (at 0x1080b52-0x1080b9f), repeated 16x per iter — these byte stores cannot coalesce, capping bandwidth at 23% of ceiling. Scalar loads (vmovss DWORD PTR [rcx-0x8]) on stride-68 deliver only 4-12 useful bytes per line.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.997-1.16x baseline at every N×q point and 2.0-3.7x slower than the winner. The scalar codegen (13 scalar-only vector ops, 199 insns/iter in loop 2, 16x byte-granular scatter in loop 3) cannot stream: 2.96 GB/s is 23% of ceiling against a 5.359 ns/p floor. The 63-68% backend-stall and 10-15% branch-flush shares confirm overhead-bound execution, and the flat ns/p-vs-N curve across all cache regimes proves cache behavior is irrelevant when instruction latency dominates. Halide AOT delegation of loop 1 alone cannot compensate for scalar respawn and render.
